name: Contract Definer
description: Workflow that generates a Maestro contract from a natural language description.

contract-structure.description: Generated contract has all required fields and proper structure

tests.description: Contract contains id, features, requiredCapabilities, minimumFitness
tests.prompt: A greeting agent that says hello and remembers user names across conversations

tests.description: Contract features have weight and minimumScore
tests.prompt: A code reviewer that checks for bugs, security issues, and style violations in TypeScript code
An agent that translates English to French with proper grammar and tone preservation
A commit message writer that reads git diffs and produces conventional commits

contract-quality.description: Generated contracts have meaningful content, not just structure

tests.description: Contract declares appropriate capabilities for the described task
tests.prompt: An agent that reads source code files, runs shell commands to execute tests, and writes test result reports

tests.description: Contract defines more than one feature for a complex description
tests.prompt: A full-stack code reviewer that checks frontend React components for accessibility, backend Node.js APIs for security, and database queries for performance

tests.description: Tests in the contract use different check types
tests.prompt: An agent that creates project documentation, including README files and API docs, and validates the output format

tests.description: Contract sets a minimumFitness value between 0 and 1
tests.prompt: A simple echo agent that repeats back whatever the user says

description-adaptation.description: Contract adapts to different types of block descriptions

tests.description: Produces a contract even for a very simple description
Produces a rich contract for a detailed description
tests.prompt: A Kubernetes deployment agent that reads YAML manifests, validates them against best practices (resource limits, liveness probes, security contexts), generates helm charts, and runs dry-run deployments. It should support multiple environments (dev, staging, prod) and rollback on failure.

tests.description: Identifies tool-calling capability for tool-heavy descriptions
tests.prompt: An agent that uses file-read to analyze code, shell-execute to run linters, file-write to generate reports, and git commands to create branches

tests.description: Identifies conversation capability for chat-focused descriptions
tests.prompt: A customer support chatbot that answers questions about Maestro, explains concepts, and helps troubleshoot issues through multi-turn dialogue
